# Health, Safety and Emergencies
Laboratories carry risks that offices don't. Read this page before you start work, and follow it every time.
In any emergency, [bold]Corporate Security is in charge[/bold]. Do what they tell you.
## Everyday lab safety - Wear your lab coat, gloves and eye protection whenever you're handling chemicals or samples. - Know where the nearest emergency shower and medical kit are. - Never taste, sniff or touch an unknown substance. - Clean up spills straight away. If you don't know what was spilled, leave the room, close the door and tell the Lead Researcher. - Report every injury, however small, and get it seen to by medical staff.
## Containment breach If a specimen gets loose, or you suspect it has: 1. [bold]Get out.[/bold] Leave the lab immediately. Don't try to recapture it and don't stop for your work. 2. [bold]Seal the area.[/bold] Close and lock the doors behind you if you can do it safely. 3. [bold]Call it in.[/bold] Report it on the Company radio channel: what got out, where it was last seen and whether anyone is hurt. 4. [bold]Stay away.[/bold] Wait somewhere secure until Security tells you it's safe. Don't go back in for anything.
Don't discuss a containment breach on any open channel, and don't tell colonial staff what escaped. If colonists are at risk, Security will warn them.
## Exposure If you think you've been exposed to a specimen's blood, venom, spores or tissue, report it at once and get to medical staff. Don't wait for symptoms. Early treatment saves lives, and the Company keeps treatments for some exposures. Tell medical staff it's a laboratory exposure and the Company will handle the rest.
## If the site comes under threat If the site itself is attacked, follow the same procedure as office staff: 1. [bold]Get away[/bold] if you can do it safely. 2. [bold]Lock yourself in[/bold] if you can't. Stay quiet and keep away from doors and windows. 3. [bold]Call it in[/bold] on the Company radio channel. 4. [bold]Wait[/bold] for Security to tell you it's safe.
If you have time before you leave, lock away samples and sensitive data. Don't put yourself in danger to do it.
## Evacuation If the site is evacuated, go where Security tells you and stay with the group. Research staff and their data have priority for any Company shuttle. Be there on time, because the shuttle can't wait.
## After an incident Write down what happened while it's fresh and give it to the Lead Researcher. Don't discuss it with anyone else.
